## Local MCP Demo — Introduction

This documentation set supports the demo workspace for the MCP server. According to the supplied README, it is intentionally small but complete enough to showcase modern MCP usage with runtime guardrails.

The README does not name individual tools; it lists these capability areas:

- **Discovery, invocation, and reads** — tool discovery and invocation flows, plus resource listing and reads.
- **Search** — structured search and grep workflows.
- **Writes and guardrails** — safe write operations in a bounded workspace, and guardrail behavior for invalid and risky inputs.

It also outlines four core runtime concepts: transport-layer MCP endpoints under `/mcp/v1/*`; a registry layer for tools and resources; a security layer covering path validation, read-only enforcement, and file-size controls; and request guardrails for bounded body size and request rate.

Recommended reading order is `guide.md`, then `walkthrough.md`, then `scenarios.md`. Named tools, endpoints, and resources are cataloged in `../../docs/mcp-reference.md`; the README also points to `../../docs/security-model.md` (security boundaries and assumptions) and `../../docs/production-deployment.md` (deployment hardening). Those files are referenced but not included in the supplied documentation, so no specific tools are named here.
